title: Gen Z and Millennials Choose Different Travel Spots
paragraphs: Deciding where to go on vacation can be hard, but a new study has found that your age might be making the decision for you!

New data from the UK travel company Adventure360 shows that Gen Z — people born in the late 1990s and early 2000s — and Millennials, those born from the early 1980s to the mid-1990s, are traveling to different places.

Adventure360 looked at over 4,700 bookings made by Gen Z and Millennial travelers between August 2025 and August 2026. It then ranked the countries based on the percentage of bookings that they were included in.

For Gen Z, Thailand was the clear favorite, included in 29.2% of bookings. Australia came second, followed by Indonesia and Vietnam. Cambodia, Laos and New Zealand were also in the top 10 for Gen Z, but not for Millennials.

For Millennials, Australia came out on top, included in 17.8% of bookings. Thailand was a close second, followed by the Philippines and Japan. Greece and Iceland were also in the top 10, but did not appear on the Gen Z list.
A few factors may help explain these differences.
One may be money. Gen Z seems to prefer cheaper destinations such as Thailand, Cambodia and Laos, while Millennials seem more willing to spend extra on trips to places like Japan and Iceland.

Social media may also be a bigger influence for Gen Z than for Millennials, with previous research by Skyscanner showing that 88% of Gen Z travelers follow at least one TikTok travel influencer. Places like Koh Rong's Long Beach in Cambodia and the Kuang Si waterfalls in Laos have gone viral this year, which might partly explain Gen Z's interest in those countries.
So the next time you can't agree with a friend on where to go on vacation, blame it on your birth year!
